Campaign brief: Resend gives this engineer a documented custom-SMTP route for Supabase Auth, with clear sending limits and a concrete setup path before authentication email volume becomes a launch constraint.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: Resend gives this engineer a documented custom-SMTP route for Supabase Auth, with clear sending limits and a concrete setup path before authentication email volume becomes a launch constraint.
events.arc: Move in one email from the recognizable risk of built-in auth-email limits, to the launch of Resend as a documented custom-SMTP option, to the limits that still require attention, and finally to the Supabase-specific setup guide.

emails.job: Get the reader to review the Supabase-specific SMTP setup and decide whether Resend should become the sender for authentication email before the next launch or volume increase.
emails.single_idea: Resend is now available as a documented sending layer for Supabase Auth, giving teams an alternative to relying on the built-in email provider when signup, OTP, magic-link, and invite volume begins to exceed its limits.
emails.objection: Will custom SMTP actually remove the limit, or simply replace it with another one?
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend changes or bypasses Supabase’s own Auth rate-limit setting; it must be adjusted separately.
Do not imply the Resend Free plan removes sending ceilings; it is limited to 100 emails per day and 3,000 per month.
Do not promise to detect or survive Supabase silently clearing its SMTP configuration.
Do not claim to explain or correct how Supabase meters requests against its limits.
Do not promise uninterrupted authentication email, guaranteed inbox placement, or a specific deliverability result.
Do not claim transactional and marketing sending are isolated by account or infrastructure; IP-level isolation requires a qualifying Scale plan and dedicated-IP add-on.
Do not broaden the email into Broadcasts, Automations, Templates, dedicated IPs, security, compliance, customer-logo lists, or the full SDK catalog.
Do not describe Resend as faster, broader, higher quality, effortless, or more controllable than every alternative.
Do not manufacture urgency, scarcity, or a deadline.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: The hosted auth plan upgrade does not itself replace the built-in sender. Custom SMTP must be configured, and Supabase applies a separate initial limit of 30 authentication messages per hour that must be adjusted in its rate-limit settings.
emails.mechanism: Resend provides Supabase-specific SMTP instructions. The engineer verifies a domain, creates a Resend API key, enters Resend’s SMTP credentials in Supabase, and separately sets the appropriate Supabase Auth rate limit. Resend Free remains capped at 100 emails per day; Pro has no daily email limit.
emails.call_to_action: Read the Supabase SMTP setup guide — https://resend.com/docs/send-with-supabase-smtp
emails.next_step_decision: Whether Resend’s documented SMTP route is technically appropriate for the team’s Supabase Auth email before choosing a plan or changing production traffic.
emails.next_step_value: The guide provides the concrete path for enabling Resend as Supabase’s custom SMTP provider and entering the required credentials.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading or completing the SMTP setup does not automatically raise Supabase’s initial 30-messages-per-hour limit, remove Resend plan quotas, or prove production deliverability.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: The reader does not need to commit to a full migration to learn whether Resend fits; they can start by connecting and testing one defined email path.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: Treating evaluation as an all-at-once migration makes the first decision larger than necessary.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Resend exposes SMTP credentials through an API key and provides a Supabase-specific configuration path, so the engineer can scope an initial test to one email flow. Raycast reported completing a separate waitlist-email test within 30 minutes after switching from SendGrid, which supports testing a narrow path but does not establish a complete migration time.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating Resend requires committing to a full provider migration. After: one bounded email flow can be used to test the documented connection before a broader decision.
must_not_say: Do not promise that a full migration takes 30 minutes.
Do not imply that Raycast’s test used Supabase Auth.
Do not claim that generating a Resend API key automatically changes Supabase rate limits.
Do not promise unchanged production behavior or guaranteed deliverability.
alternative_arguments.objection: Switching sending providers sounds like a project I do not have time for.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Whether to configure a bounded Supabase Auth email test with Resend before considering a broader migration.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The official page documents this verified fact: Resend SMTP requires its host, an approved port, the fixed username, and a Resend API key as the password.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: Creating the key does not verify the domain, change Supabase’s rate-limit setting, prove production deliverability, or establish how long a complete migration will take.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the launch as a small, concrete first test for Supabase Auth rather than a wholesale email migration.
